nodes.summary: A binomial family whose success probability lies in `[0, 1]` and is monotone on `S` has a monotone likelihood ratio on `S`.
nodes.title: Binomial family has monotone likelihood ratio

nodes.summary: Binomial likelihood with `N` trials and parameter-dependent success probability `p θ`: `L n θ = C(N, n) p θ ^ n (1 - p θ) ^ (N - n)` (zero for `n > N`, since `C(N, n) = 0`).
nodes.title: Binomial likelihood

nodes.summary: The likelihood family has an antitone likelihood ratio on `S`: `L` is nonnegative on `S`, and for `n ≤ m` and `θ ≤ θ'` in `S`, `L n θ * L m θ' ≤ L m θ * L n θ'`. For positive likelihoods this says `θ ↦ L m θ / L n θ` is nonincreasing (larger counts favor smaller parameters).
nodes.title: Antitone likelihood ratio

nodes.summary: The likelihood family `L : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ` (observation, parameter) has a monotone likelihood ratio on the parameter set `S`: `L` is nonnegative on `S`, and for observations `n ≤ m` and parameters `θ ≤ θ'` in `S`, `L m θ * L n θ' ≤ L n θ * L m θ'` (total positivity of order two). For positive likelihoods this is monotonicity of `θ ↦ L m θ / L n θ`. The nonnegativity is part of the predicate: without it the downstream…
nodes.title: Monotone likelihood ratio

nodes.summary: A Poisson family whose mean is nonnegative and antitone on `S` has an antitone likelihood ratio on `S`.
nodes.title: Poisson family with antitone mean has antitone likelihood ratio

nodes.summary: A Poisson family whose mean is nonnegative and monotone on `S` has a monotone likelihood ratio on `S`.
nodes.title: Poisson family with monotone mean has monotone likelihood ratio

nodes.summary: Poisson likelihood with parameter-dependent mean `λ θ`: `L n θ = e^{-λ θ} λ θ ^ n / (n !)`.
nodes.title: Poisson likelihood

nodes.summary: The posterior is stochastically nonincreasing in the observation for a family with an antitone likelihood ratio and every prior: if `n ≤ m` and both marginal likelihoods are positive, then `P(θ > t ∣ m) ≤ P(θ > t ∣ n)` for every `t`.
nodes.title: The posterior is stochastically nonincreasing in the observation

nodes.summary: The posterior is stochastically nondecreasing in the observation for an MLR family and every prior (Milgrom 1981, Prop. 2): if `n ≤ m` and both marginal likelihoods are positive, then `P(θ > t ∣ n) ≤ P(θ > t ∣ m)` for every `t`.
nodes.title: The posterior is stochastically nondecreasing in the observation

nodes.summary: Posterior probability of `{θ > t}` after observing `n`, by Bayes' formula for the prior `μ` and likelihood `L`: `(∫_{θ > t} L n θ dμ) / ∫ L n θ dμ`. Meaningful when the marginal likelihood `∫ L n dμ` is positive (otherwise the division returns the junk value `0`), and a genuine posterior probability only when `L` is nonnegative (as in the MLR predicates: a signed `L` can give a value outside `[0, 1]`).
nodes.title: Posterior tail probability

nodes.summary: Under the hypotheses of `setIntegral_Ioi_mul_integral_le_of_hasMLR` with the reversed ratio condition, for `n ≤ m`: `(∫_{θ > t} L m dμ) (∫ L n dμ) ≤ (∫_{θ > t} L n dμ) (∫ L m dμ)`.
nodes.title: Posterior stochastic ordering for an antitone likelihood ratio, cross-multiplied form

nodes.summary: Posterior stochastic ordering, cross-multiplied form (Milgrom 1981, Prop. 1). If the family `L` has a monotone likelihood ratio on a set `S` carrying the prior `μ` (`μ Sᶜ = 0`), and every `L n` is `μ`-integrable, then for `n ≤ m` and every threshold `t`, `(∫_{θ > t} L n dμ) (∫ L m dμ) ≤ (∫_{θ > t} L m dμ) (∫ L n dμ)`.
nodes.title: Posterior stochastic ordering, cross-multiplied form
